title: The Death of Yugoslavia: 15-day road itinerary

trip.transport: Rental-car road loop with local walking; no internal flights planned.
trip.historical_focus: The political breakup and wars of 1990–95, with Tito's Yugoslavia as context and Belgrade's 1999 bombing sites as an epilogue.
trip.organizing_principle: Geographic continuity rather than strict historical chronology.
trip.planning_status: Proposed itinerary; transport, accommodation, site access and travel dates are not booked.
trip.rental_car_note: Confirm written authorization and required insurance documents for Croatia, Slovenia, Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina.
trip.pacing_note: Days 3, 7, 10, 12 and 14 involve substantial travel. Day 13 combines remaining Mostar visits with Dubrovnik. An evening departure supports day 15.

data_conventions.sequence: Trip-wide correlative number, starting at 1, including optional stops.
data_conventions.day_stop_sequence: Correlative number within the day, starting at 1, including optional stops.
data_conventions.default_route_sequence: Consecutive number for included-by-default stops; null for optional stops.
data_conventions.default_progression: Follow route.default_stop_ids in order; optional stops are listed separately.
data_conventions.coordinate_precision_note: Coordinates are sourced map references. Decimal precision does not establish survey accuracy or visitor entrance access.
data_conventions.site_coordinate_note: The stop coordinate anchors its primary mapped feature or explicitly labeled locality/corridor. Associated sites do not receive an invented identical coordinate.
data_conventions.asset_paths: All image paths are relative to this JSON file, in the same directory.
data_conventions.image_semantics: One representative image per trip day, reused by that day's stops. Illustrations are not evidence of current conditions.
data_conventions.transport_geometry: Legs define stop-to-stop connections only. Road geometry, road distances and travel times are null because no road-routing service has been used.
data_conventions.optional_stop_handling: Optional stops have included_by_default=false and are absent from the default progression. Add them explicitly if selected.

days.title: Zagreb: political separation
days.summary: Begin with Croatia's political separation and a light arrival-day introduction.
days.pacing_notes: Light day; Mirogoj depends on arrival time.

days.title: Ljubljana: independence and Yugoslav history
days.summary: Introduce Slovenia's departure and the broader history behind the Ten-Day War.

days.title: Medvedjek and arrival in Vukovar
days.summary: Move from Slovenia's short conflict to the Croatian war in eastern Slavonia.
days.pacing_notes: Long cross-country transfer; keep Medvedjek focused.

days.title: Vukovar: siege, hospital and Ovčara
days.summary: Give the siege and hospital-to-Ovčara history a full day.
days.pacing_notes: Borovo Selo is optional; prioritize the hospital and both Ovčara locations.

days.title: Belgrade: the federation and Tito
days.summary: Reconstruct the institutions and memory of Yugoslavia after visiting Vukovar.
days.pacing_notes: Cross-border rental-car authorization and museum access require confirmation.

days.title: Belgrade: politics and the 1999 epilogue
days.summary: Examine Serbia's political center and sites connected to the 1999 bombing.
days.pacing_notes: The Kosovo war is introduced indirectly; Kosovo itself is outside this route.

days.title: Eastern Bosnia and arrival in Sarajevo
days.summary: Connect the Drina landscape and wartime political geography to Sarajevo.
days.pacing_notes: Long transfer with a substantive Višegrad stop.

days.title: Sarajevo: civilian life under siege
days.summary: Use the museum and central urban sites to examine civilian survival and destruction.
days.pacing_notes: War Childhood Museum is optional according to time and emotional bandwidth.

days.title: Sarajevo: the siege perimeter
days.summary: Relate the airport, tunnel and heights to the military geometry of the siege.
days.pacing_notes: Use established public access routes and paths.

days.title: Potočari and Srebrenica
days.summary: Give the genocide memorial and former Dutchbat compound sustained attention.
days.pacing_notes: Allocate several hours to the memorial; arrange guided access if desired.

days.title: Tuzla and the Prijedor camp landscape
days.summary: Connect civilian attacks, detention, displacement and contested remembrance.
days.pacing_notes: Keraterm is an optional exterior visit; Omarska requires a separate access arrangement.

days.title: Central Bosnia and Mostar
days.summary: Introduce the Croat–Bosniak conflict and Mostar's divided urban landscape.
days.pacing_notes: A substantial driving day; the Mostar museum and bridge follow the next morning.

days.title: Mostar and Dubrovnik
days.summary: Complete the essential Mostar visits and add the Dubrovnik campaign.
days.pacing_notes: Compressed day; prioritize Fort Imperial and the Old Town over outlying excursions.

days.title: Knin and the northbound return
days.summary: Examine Operation Storm and the Krajina endgame before reaching the final overnight base.
days.pacing_notes: Long driving day; check the fortress's seasonal opening.

days.title: Plitvice and Zagreb Airport
days.summary: Return to an early Croatian-war site and close the airport loop.
days.pacing_notes: An evening flight supports this schedule; park and Turanj visits are optional.

presentation.title: The Death of Yugoslavia
presentation.subtitle: A 15-day road journey through the breakup of a country.

map.connection_note: Connections show travel order, not driving directions.

cards.title: Zagreb: political separation
cards.text: Begin with Croatia's political separation and a light arrival-day introduction.

cards.title: St. Mark's Square and Croatian Parliament
cards.text: Croatia's Parliament adopted its sovereignty and independence decision on 25 June 1991. St. Mark's Square places that political break within the compact government district, before the route turns to the landscapes of the war.

cards.title: Mirogoj Cemetery
cards.text: Franjo Tuđman's tomb introduces the president whose political project shaped independent Croatia. Mirogoj also offers an early encounter with the national remembrance that frames later visits to Vukovar and Knin.

cards.title: Ljubljana: independence and Yugoslav history
cards.text: Introduce Slovenia's departure and the broader history behind the Ten-Day War.

cards.title: Republic Square and National Assembly
cards.text: Slovenia's independence was ceremonially proclaimed in Republic Square on 26 June 1991. The National Assembly stands beside the square, giving the journey a second perspective on the federation's political dissolution.

cards.title: Contemporary history museum at Cekin Mansion
cards.text: The museum's permanent exhibition follows Slovenian life through the twentieth century to independence in 1991. Its account of the socialist period gives the short independence war a longer institutional and social context.

cards.title: Medvedjek and arrival in Vukovar
cards.text: Move from Slovenia's short conflict to the Croatian war in eastern Slavonia.

cards.title: Medvedjek Ten-Day War landscape
cards.text: A Yugoslav People's Army column encountered a blockade at Medvedjek during the Ten-Day War. The 1991 memorial links the political departure seen in Ljubljana with the armed conflict along the road east.

cards.title: Vukovar Water Tower
cards.text: The damaged water tower became a defining image of Vukovar's 1991 siege. An arrival-day visit introduces the city and the Danube landscape before the following day's more sustained examination of its wartime history.

cards.title: Vukovar: siege, hospital and Ovčara
cards.text: Give the siege and hospital-to-Ovčara history a full day.

cards.title: Borovo Selo
cards.text: The confrontation at Borovo Selo in May 1991 preceded the full siege of Vukovar. The village provides an earlier point in the local sequence of violence, before the hospital and Ovčara visits.

cards.title: Trpinjska Road Memorial Home
cards.text: Trpinjska Road was a major defensive sector during the battle for Vukovar. The memorial home occupies the site of the former command post and presents the defenders' account of the fighting in this part of the city.

cards.title: Vukovar Hospital 1991 memorial
cards.text: The hospital continued treating people under bombardment throughout the siege. Its basement memorial preserves the conditions of that work and prepares the connection to Ovčara, where people taken from the hospital were detained and killed.

cards.title: Homeland War Memorial Center
cards.text: The memorial center presents the battle through exhibitions and military material. Read its account alongside the hospital and other physical sites, noting how the siege is interpreted within Croatian national remembrance.

cards.title: Vukovar Water Tower siege visit
cards.text: Return to the water tower as part of the full siege visit. The additional time allows its commemorative interpretation to be considered alongside the hospital, defensive sectors and memorial center.

cards.title: Ovčara Memorial Home
cards.text: The memorial home occupies the former farm hangar where people removed from Vukovar Hospital were detained. Visiting it after the hospital connects the urban siege to the violence in the agricultural landscape outside the city.

cards.title: Ovčara mass-grave memorial
cards.text: The mass-grave memorial is a separate location from the former hangar. It completes the hospital-to-Ovčara sequence at the landscape of burial, exhumation and remembrance.

cards.title: Belgrade: the federation and Tito
cards.text: Reconstruct the institutions and memory of Yugoslavia after visiting Vukovar.

cards.title: Museum of Yugoslavia and House of Flowers
cards.text: The Museum of Yugoslavia and Tito's House of Flowers turn the journey back toward the state that was breaking apart. Its collections and Tito's tomb provide context for the federation's institutions, public culture and political memory.

cards.title: Sava Centar
cards.text: The final extraordinary congress of the League of Communists met in Belgrade in January 1990. Sava Centar connects that collapse of the common party with the monumental architecture of the federal capital.

cards.title: Palace of Serbia and federal district
cards.text: The Palace of Serbia was built for the federal government. Its scale and position in New Belgrade express the institutional ambitions of socialist Yugoslavia and provide a setting for considering the loss of federal authority.

cards.title: Belgrade: politics and the 1999 epilogue
cards.text: Examine Serbia's political center and sites connected to the 1999 bombing.

cards.title: National Assembly and political center
cards.text: The National Assembly places the Serbian political center within the journey. The visit helps distinguish Serbia's republican institutions from the federal structures encountered elsewhere in Belgrade.

cards.title: Republic Square
cards.text: Republic Square provides an urban setting for examining public politics in Belgrade. Use the walk through the center to connect institutional history with the city's public spaces.

cards.title: RTS bombing memorial
cards.text: NATO bombed the Radio Television of Serbia building on 23 April 1999, killing sixteen employees. The memorial introduces civilian loss and the continuing public remembrance of the attack.

cards.title: Former General Staff complex
cards.text: The bomb-damaged General Staff complex connects federal military architecture with the 1999 NATO campaign. It serves as a later chapter in this journey; the Kosovo war itself would require a separate extension.

cards.title: Eastern Bosnia and arrival in Sarajevo
cards.text: Connect the Drina landscape and wartime political geography to Sarajevo.

cards.title: Mehmed Paša Sokolović Bridge
cards.text: The bridge and Drina riverfront belong to a landscape of expulsion and killings of Bosniak civilians in 1992. The stop connects the journey through eastern Bosnia to the human history of the places along the road.

cards.title: Pale wartime political landscape
cards.text: Pale was the wartime Bosnian Serb political center. Passing through the mountain town before descending into Sarajevo connects that political geography with the enclosed city below.

cards.title: Arrival in Sarajevo
cards.text: The approach through eastern Bosnia and Pale ends in Sarajevo. The next two days examine the city at two scales: civilian life in its streets and the surrounding geography that sustained the siege.

cards.title: Sarajevo: civilian life under siege
cards.text: Use the museum and central urban sites to examine civilian survival and destruction.

cards.title: History Museum and Besieged Sarajevo
cards.text: The Besieged Sarajevo exhibition uses everyday objects, photographs and improvised equipment to examine civilian life under siege. It provides a grounding before the walk through the central urban sites.

cards.title: Former Holiday Inn and Sniper Alley
cards.text: The former Holiday Inn and the boulevard known as Sniper Alley connect wartime reporting with the exposure of people moving through Sarajevo. The surrounding streets make the city's siege geography visible at ground level.

cards.title: Markale Market
cards.text: Markale places the history of attacks on civilians within an ordinary market setting. Nearby Sarajevo Roses mark other locations of wartime deaths within the city's everyday street surfaces.

cards.title: Vijećnica
cards.text: Vijećnica connects the siege to the destruction of civic and cultural institutions. Its rebuilding also makes it a place to consider what reconstruction preserves and how the city presents that history.

cards.title: War Childhood Museum
cards.text: The War Childhood Museum presents children's wartime experiences through personal objects and testimony. It adds an individual perspective to the military and institutional geography examined elsewhere in Sarajevo.

cards.title: Sarajevo: the siege perimeter
cards.text: Relate the airport, tunnel and heights to the military geometry of the siege.

cards.title: Tunnel of Hope and airport perimeter
cards.text: The Tunnel of Hope passed beneath the airport runway, linking besieged Sarajevo with territory that could supply the city. The airport's position is essential to understanding why this connection mattered.

cards.title: Dobrinja siege geography
cards.text: Dobrinja connects the tunnel and airport visit to the residential neighborhoods affected by the siege. The neighborhood makes the relationship between homes, front lines and access routes more concrete.

cards.title: Vraca Memorial Park
cards.text: Vraca combines a Yugoslav antifascist memorial landscape with a position on the heights above Sarajevo. It brings two periods of conflict and remembrance into the same part of the city.

cards.title: Old Jewish Cemetery
cards.text: The old Jewish cemetery occupies sloping ground overlooking Sarajevo. Its position connects a historic burial landscape with the military geography of the siege.

cards.title: Trebević Olympic bobsled track
cards.text: The 1984 Olympic track belongs to the heights used during the siege. It connects the city's international Olympic image with the war that followed less than a decade later.

cards.title: Potočari and Srebrenica
cards.text: Give the genocide memorial and former Dutchbat compound sustained attention.

cards.title: Srebrenica-Potočari memorial cemetery
cards.text: The cemetery at Potočari commemorates victims of the July 1995 Srebrenica genocide. Give this place sustained attention before continuing to the exhibitions across the road.

cards.title: Former Dutchbat compound
cards.text: The former battery factory housed the Dutch UN battalion. Its exhibitions connect the physical compound with the declared safe area, the genocide and the international failure to protect the population.

cards.title: Srebrenica town
cards.text: Continue into Srebrenica to place the memorial within the town and surrounding enclave. This links Potočari's cemetery and exhibitions with the urban landscape to which their history refers.

cards.title: Arrival in Tuzla
cards.text: Continue to Tuzla for the night rather than returning to Sarajevo. The northwestward journey positions the next morning's Kapija visit and the route toward Prijedor.

cards.title: Tuzla and the Prijedor camp landscape
cards.text: Connect civilian attacks, detention, displacement and contested remembrance.

cards.title: Kapija memorial
cards.text: An attack on Kapija on 25 May 1995 killed people gathered in Tuzla's central public space. The memorial begins the day with civilian remembrance before the journey toward the Prijedor camp landscape.

cards.title: Kozarac
cards.text: Kozarac connects the Prijedor detention camps with the surrounding communities affected by destruction and displacement. The town also introduces the history of return after the war.

cards.title: Former Trnopolje camp
cards.text: The Trnopolje camp occupied school and community buildings. Its surviving landscape connects detention and forced displacement with the continuing difficulties of marking and interpreting these sites.

cards.title: Former Keraterm camp exterior
cards.text: The former Keraterm factory was used as a detention camp. An exterior visit offers a comparison with Trnopolje, where civic buildings were converted to the same purpose.

cards.title: Prijedor town and overnight base
cards.text: The camp sites belong to the wider history of the takeover of Prijedor and the removal of its non-Serb population. The town provides the overnight base before the journey into central Bosnia.

cards.title: Central Bosnia and Mostar
cards.text: Introduce the Croat–Bosniak conflict and Mostar's divided urban landscape.

cards.title: Ahmići massacre memorial landscape
cards.text: The massacre at Ahmići on 16 April 1993 is central to understanding the Croat–Bosniak conflict. The village and its memorial landscape complicate an account of the Bosnian war limited to Serb–Bosniak fighting.

cards.title: Vitez and the Lašva Valley
cards.text: Vitez places Ahmići within the wider Lašva Valley conflict. A brief stop connects the village visit with the nearby town and the geography of central Bosnia.

cards.title: Mostar Bulevar division
cards.text: The Bulevar formed a principal wartime division in Mostar. Begin the city visit here to connect its present urban landscape with the Croat–Bosniak conflict.

cards.title: Stari Most evening orientation
cards.text: An evening walk reaches Stari Most after the Bulevar. The bridge introduces the destruction and reconstruction examined more closely in the following morning's visit.

cards.title: Mostar and Dubrovnik
cards.text: Complete the essential Mostar visits and add the Dubrovnik campaign.

cards.title: Stari Most and Mostar war history
cards.text: Stari Most's destruction and reconstruction connect Mostar's most recognizable landmark with the war. Complete the essential Old Town visit before the photographic exhibition and the journey to Dubrovnik.

cards.title: War Photo Museum Mostar 1992–1995
cards.text: The museum's photographs follow Mostar through the 1992–95 war. They connect the bridge and former front line with the destruction and civilian experiences represented in the collection.

cards.title: Fort Imperial and Mount Srđ
cards.text: Fort Imperial stood on Dubrovnik's defense line and housed a Croatian brigade headquarters. Its museum explains the campaign and the destruction below, while the view makes the relationship between the heights and Old Town clear.

cards.title: Dubrovnik Old Town
cards.text: Return from Srđ to the city affected by the 1991 attack. The Old Town and Sponza Palace memorial room connect the military overview with individual loss and damage to the urban fabric.

cards.title: Knin and the northbound return
cards.text: Examine Operation Storm and the Krajina endgame before reaching the final overnight base.

cards.title: Knin Fortress and Operation Storm exhibition
cards.text: Knin Fortress contains an exhibition on Operation Storm in 1995. The visit examines the military endgame in the Krajina and the place it occupies in Croatian national remembrance.

cards.title: Korenica overnight base
cards.text: Continue north from Knin to Korenica for the final overnight stay. This positions the last day's Plitvice visit before the return to Zagreb Airport.

cards.title: Plitvice and Zagreb Airport
cards.text: Return to an early Croatian-war site and close the airport loop.

cards.title: Josip Jović / Bloody Easter memorial
cards.text: The Josip Jović memorial recalls the clash at Plitvice on 31 March 1991. The journey returns to an early episode of the Croatian war before closing the airport loop.

cards.title: Plitvice Lakes limited park visit
cards.text: A limited park visit can accompany the historical stop if the departure schedule allows. Keep the walking time flexible so the journey to Zagreb Airport retains a sufficient buffer.

cards.title: Homeland War Museum at Turanj
cards.text: The museum at Turanj examines the war in the Karlovac region. It connects the final drive with a contested corridor between northern Croatia and the coast.

cards.title: Zagreb Airport departure
cards.text: Return the car at Zagreb Airport to complete the loop. The itinerary assumes an evening departure; earlier flights require the final visits to be shortened.
